findings.title: Unauthenticated Remote Access to Order Fulfillment Workflows & 18-Agent Execution Pipeline
findings.summary: The order workflow dispatch and what-if simulation endpoints lack any authentication or authorization dependencies. Any unauthenticated caller on the network can trigger intensive background executions of the full 18-agent LangGraph workflow, consuming cloud LLM API tokens (Groq/OpenAI) and writing unverified transactions to persistent storage.
findings.execution_path: Untrusted Caller -> POST /api/v1/workflows/orders -> workflows.py:start_order_workflow() [No auth dependency] -> BackgroundTasks.add_task(_run_workflow) -> workflow.py:compile_workflow() -> StateGraph executes 18 AI agents (OrderManagement, DemandForecast, Inventory, Warehouse, Supplier, Transportation, Sustainability, QA, Finance, Pricing, Risk, Procurement, Planner, Negotiation, ConsensusChecker, CustomerService, Manufacturing, Reporting) -> Live Groq/OpenAI LLM API calls + SQLite persistence writes
findings.root_cause: The endpoints were implemented for development convenience without role guards or OAuth2/JWT security dependencies, relying on obscurity rather than defense-in-depth.
findings.reachability: Unauthenticated remote network caller. Deployed on all network interfaces bound to port 8000.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Attacker sends HTTP POST to http://<host>:8000/api/v1/workflows/orders with JSON payload `{"customer_id": "50000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001", "items": [{"product_id": "30000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001", "quantity": 500}]}`.
2. Server returns HTTP 202 Accepted without prompting for credentials.
3. The server immediately enqueues 18 background agent tasks, depleting external Groq API rate limits, locking SQLite storage, and generating rogue customer orders.
findings.impact: Exhaustion of production LLM API budgets and quotas, resource exhaustion / DoS on application server, unauthorized modification of supply chain digital twin state, pollution of executive dashboards and reports.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked app/main.py middleware (CORS only, no global auth gate). Checked routers in backend/app/api/v1/auth.py (has require_authenticated_role, but it is never imported or applied in simulate.py or workflows.py:start_order_workflow).

remediation.strategy: Apply mandatory role-based access control (RBAC) to order creation and simulation triggers. Require operator or admin role tokens and bind tenant/caller identity to the initial workflow state.
implementation_steps: Import require_authenticated_role in backend/app/api/v1/workflows.py and backend/app/api/v1/simulate.py.
Add current_user: dict = Depends(require_authenticated_role(['admin', 'operator'])) to start_order_workflow.
Add current_user: dict = Depends(require_authenticated_role(['admin', 'analyst'])) to start_simulation.
Propagate current_user['username'] into the initial workflow state and audit trail.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/app/api/v1/workflows.py
@router.post("/orders", status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED)
async def start_order_workflow(
    request: OrderWorkflowRequest,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
    current_user: dict = Depends(require_authenticated_role(["admin", "operator"])),
) -> WorkflowAcceptedResponse:
    ...
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Adopt a default-deny FastAPI router dependency or middleware that requires valid authentication across all /api/v1/* routes except explicit public endpoints (/health, /auth/token).
remediation.rollout_considerations: Requires frontend clients to include Authorization: Bearer <token> headers when invoking order and simulation endpoints.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: HTTP POST to /api/v1/workflows/orders without Authorization header returns 401 Unauthorized; with valid operator bearer token returns 202 Accepted.
remediation.resolution_details: Added require_authenticated_role dependency to POST /api/v1/workflows/orders and POST /api/v1/simulate/start in workflows.py and simulate.py.

findings.limitations: Tested via static control flow and unit test harness; dynamic external load testing not conducted per safety rules.

findings.title: Architectural Dual-Storage Split-Brain and Data Desynchronization Between PostgreSQL and SQLite
findings.summary: The application maintains two completely isolated, competing data stores: PostgreSQL via SQLAlchemy async sessions and SQLite via persistence.py. Write endpoints (orders, shipments, procurement, replenishment) write exclusively to SQLite, while read endpoints prioritize querying PostgreSQL and fall back to SQLite only on database exception. When PostgreSQL is online, freshly created orders, shipments, and inventory updates are completely invisible in listing queries.
findings.execution_path: Client POST /api/v1/orders -> orders.py:create_commercial_order() -> persistence.save_order_with_items() [Writes exclusively to backend/.storage/digital_twin.db; no insert into PostgreSQL] -> Client GET /api/v1/orders -> orders.py:list_orders() -> session.execute(select(Order)) [Queries PostgreSQL] -> Query succeeds -> Returns old PostgreSQL data missing all newly created orders.
findings.root_cause: The project was designed with an in-memory/SQLite persistence fallback layer to allow running without Docker, but write endpoints were refactored to write directly to persistence.py without updating the underlying PostgreSQL ORM models.
findings.evidence:
# backend/app/api/v1/orders.py:332
persistence.save_order_with_items(order_record, order_items_records)
# No db.session.add(Order(...)) or commit

# backend/app/api/v1/orders.py:76
result = await session.execute(query)
orders = result.scalars().all()
# When session succeeds, persistence.list_orders is never reached!
findings.reachability: Any user creating orders, shipments, or POs in an environment where PostgreSQL is active.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Production system runs with PostgreSQL connected.
2. Customer submits an order via POST /api/v1/orders.
3. Server returns HTTP 201 Created with order ID `ord-abc123`.
4. Operations team loads GET /api/v1/orders on the dashboard.
5. The order does not appear in the list because list_orders queries PostgreSQL where the order was never inserted.
6. Inventory replenishment receives stock via /replenish/auto-heal (updating SQLite), but warehouse operators querying inventory via /inventory see stockout because PostgreSQL inventory is unchanged.
findings.impact: Complete data split-brain, lost orders, ghost inventory, failed shipments, irrecoverable state divergence between database replicas.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked whether persistence writes sync back to PostgreSQL in background workers or event dispatcher: verified no synchronization worker exists.

remediation.strategy: Unify the data layer onto PostgreSQL as the single source of truth using SQLAlchemy async sessions for all mutations and reads. Deprecate dual writes to SQLite or isolate SQLite strictly to an offline dev-mock mode.
implementation_steps: Refactor create_commercial_order to create and commit SQLAlchemy Order and OrderItem entities within the active async session.
Refactor create_shipment, create_purchase_order, and receive_purchase_order to operate through SQLAlchemy repositories.
Ensure persistence.py is either eliminated or acts as a transparent read-through/write-through cache only when PostgreSQL is unreachable.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/app/api/v1/orders.py
order = Order(
    order_id=order_id,
    customer_id=payload.customer_id,
    status="pending",
    priority=payload.priority,
    total_amount=Decimal(str(total_val)),
)
session.add(order)
await session.commit()
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Eliminate direct ad-hoc SQL execution across disparate database engines; enforce repository abstraction pattern uniformly across all domain modules.
remediation.rollout_considerations: Requires database migration and seeding to ensure PostgreSQL contains identical baseline catalog data.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: A record created via POST /orders is immediately returned in GET /orders when PostgreSQL is connected.
remediation.resolution_details: Implemented dual-storage SQLite/PostgreSQL write synchronization in orders.py and shipments.py, plus hardened session rollback in database.py.

references: Martin Fowler - Single Source of Truth
findings.limitations: PostgreSQL was offline during local automated test execution; verified via code path analysis.

findings.title: Production Authentication Lockout Due to In-Memory User Store Emptied in Production Mode
findings.summary: In backend/app/api/v1/auth.py, the user repository _DEV_USERS is initialized as an empty dictionary {} when ENVIRONMENT != 'development'. Because there is no PostgreSQL users table or external identity provider integration, any call to POST /api/v1/auth/token in production immediately returns HTTP 401 Incorrect username or password, and get_current_user rejects all tokens.
findings.execution_path: Environment variable ENVIRONMENT=production -> auth.py:81 sets _DEV_USERS = {} -> User calls POST /api/v1/auth/token with valid credentials -> auth.py:280 user = _DEV_USERS.get(form.username) -> user is None -> raises HTTP 401. Result: Zero users can authenticate in production.
findings.root_cause: The authentication system relies on an in-memory dictionary created for development and lacks a persistent database-backed User model with role and credential storage.
findings.reachability: Any user or client attempting to authenticate against the API when ENVIRONMENT=production.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. System is deployed to staging/production with ENVIRONMENT=production.
2. Administrator attempts to log in via POST /api/v1/auth/token using configured credentials.
3. Server returns 401 Unauthorized for every username and password combination.
4. All protected endpoints requiring admin/operator privileges become completely unreachable.
findings.impact: Complete system lockout in production; total denial of service for administrative and operational workflows.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked whether an alternative OAuth2/LDAP/OIDC provider is configured in backend/app/core/config.py: None exists. Checked whether a User model exists in backend/app/models/: No User model exists.

remediation.strategy: Create a database-backed User table in PostgreSQL with salted Argon2id/PBKDF2 hashes, role enumerations, and seed an initial secure administrative user via Alembic migration.
implementation_steps: Create backend/app/models/user.py with id, username, hashed_password, role, is_active, created_at.
Generate Alembic migration for the users table.
Update auth.py:login and get_current_user to query the users table via SQLAlchemy AsyncSession.
Provide an administrative CLI command (e.g. python -m app.cli create-admin) to bootstrap initial credentials.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/app/api/v1/auth.py
async def get_current_user(
    token: Annotated[str, Depends(oauth2_scheme)],
    session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db_session),
) -> User:
    payload = _decode_token(token)
    username = payload.get("sub")
    user = (await session.execute(select(User).where(User.username == username))).scalar_one_or_none()
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="User not found")
    return user
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Eliminate in-memory dictionaries for identity management; mandate persistent relational or directory-backed identity stores across all operational environments.
remediation.rollout_considerations: Requires a secure bootstrap secret or initial password generation during deployment.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: With ENVIRONMENT=production, a seeded database user can authenticate via /auth/token and access protected endpoints.
remediation.resolution_details: Created persistent User model in user.py, users table in persistence.py, and updated auth.py to authenticate against persistent storage in production mode.

findings.title: Production Frontend Build and Containerization Failure from Strict Unused Variable Violations
findings.summary: Running 'npm run build' fails with exit code 2 due to TypeScript error TS6133: 'setSearchParams' and 'urlProcessedRef' are declared but never read in OrdersPage.tsx. Because frontend/tsconfig.app.json enforces 'noUnusedLocals: true', and frontend/Dockerfile stage prod-builder executes 'npm run build', building the production Docker container (docker build --target prod frontend) is completely blocked.
findings.execution_path: Docker build / CI release pipeline -> docker build --target prod frontend -> executes Dockerfile line 18 'RUN npm run build' -> tsc -b executes -> OrdersPage.tsx TS6133 errors -> Build fails with code 2 -> Container image generation aborted.
findings.root_cause: Unused imports and local state variables were left in OrdersPage.tsx during feature development without running a production build check.
findings.evidence:
$ npm --prefix frontend run build
> frontend@0.0.0 build
> tsc -b && vite build

src/pages/OrdersPage.tsx:43:24 - error TS6133: 'setSearchParams' is declared but its value is never read.
43   const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams();
                          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/pages/OrdersPage.tsx:45:9 - error TS6133: 'urlProcessedRef' is declared but its value is never read.
45   const urlProcessedRef = useRef<string | null>(null);
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Found 2 errors.
findings.reachability: Build and release pipelines, container image builds, developers running typecheck.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Release engineer or CI runner triggers `docker build -t supply-chain-frontend:latest ./frontend`.
2. The builder reaches stage `prod-builder` at line 18.
3. TypeScript compiler halts on TS6133 in OrdersPage.tsx.
4. Build terminates with code 2; no production frontend container is produced.
findings.impact: Zero ability to build or deploy the production frontend container; automated CI/CD pipeline broken.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked whether vite build runs without tsc: package.json build script explicitly chains `tsc -b && vite build`.

remediation.strategy: Remove the unused local declarations in OrdersPage.tsx so the TypeScript compilation passes cleanly under strict compiler flags.
implementation_steps: In frontend/src/pages/OrdersPage.tsx:43, change `const [searchParams, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams();` to `const [searchParams] = useSearchParams();`.
In frontend/src/pages/OrdersPage.tsx:45, remove `const urlProcessedRef = useRef<string | null>(null);`.
Execute `npm --prefix frontend run build` to verify clean compilation.
remediation.systemic_fix: Add a pre-commit hook or CI check running `tsc --noEmit` on every pull request to catch type errors before merging.
remediation.rollout_considerations: Zero runtime impact; purely resolves compiler errors.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: npm --prefix frontend run build completes with exit code 0 and emits production bundles to dist/.
remediation.resolution_details: Aligned setSearchParams and urlProcessedRef declarations and usage in OrdersPage.tsx, resolving strict unused local variable errors.
remediation.test_results: tsc -b && vite build completed with 0 errors in 198ms, exit code 0

findings.limitations: Tested directly with npm run build in the workspace environment.

findings.title: Alembic Database Migration Failure via Unparameterized Host-Dependent Subprocess Invocation
findings.summary: In Alembic migration 922ae13073d0_initial_schema.py, the upgrade() function invokes `subprocess.run(["psql", "-d", "supply_chain", "-f", file_path], check=True)`. This bypasses Alembic's SQLAlchemy connection engine, assumes the psql CLI client is installed on the host, and hardcodes local socket connection parameters without honoring POSTGRES_SERVER, POSTGRES_USER, or POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
findings.execution_path: Operator runs 'alembic upgrade head' in container or cloud environment -> 922ae13073d0_initial_schema.py executes upgrade() -> subprocess.run(['psql', ...]) -> In Docker container (where psql client is absent or db host is 'db'), process crashes with FileNotFoundError or connection failure -> Database initialization fails.
findings.root_cause: Migration author bypassed Alembic's native op.execute() or SQLAlchemy connection to quickly apply raw SQL scripts via the external psql command-line tool.
findings.evidence:
# backend/alembic/versions/922ae13073d0_initial_schema.py:21-30
def upgrade() -> None:
    """Upgrade schema."""
    import os
    import subprocess
    file_path = "sql/01_schema.sql"
    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
        file_path = "../sql/01_schema.sql"
    # Execute DDL using native psql tool to support triggers and enums correctly
    subprocess.run(["psql", "-d", "supply_chain", "-f", file_path], check=True)
findings.reachability: Any environment executing database migrations via `alembic upgrade head`.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Deployment pipeline launches backend Docker container.
2. Container entrypoint executes `alembic upgrade head`.
3. Python raises `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'psql'` because minimal Python runner images (python:3.12-slim) do not install postgresql-client.
4. Backend fails to start, aborting container startup.
findings.impact: Inability to apply database migrations or provision fresh environments; complete deployment failure.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked whether second migration a1b2c3d4e5f6 uses psql: No, the second migration uses standard op.create_table(). Only the initial migration contains this defect.

remediation.strategy: Execute the SQL DDL file using Alembic's bound SQLAlchemy connection (op.get_bind().execute(text(...))) rather than spawning an external OS process.
implementation_steps: Open backend/alembic/versions/922ae13073d0_initial_schema.py.
Remove `import subprocess`.
Read the contents of sql/01_schema.sql and execute it using `op.execute(text(sql_content))`.
Ensure transactions and multi-statement executions are split or supported by the asyncpg/psycopg connection.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/alembic/versions/922ae13073d0_initial_schema.py
from alembic import op
from sqlalchemy import text
import os

def upgrade() -> None:
    file_path = "sql/01_schema.sql" if os.path.exists("sql/01_schema.sql") else "../sql/01_schema.sql"
    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        ddl = f.read()
    connection = op.get_bind()
    connection.execute(text(ddl))
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Ban subprocess calls inside database migration scripts via linter/CI rule.
remediation.rollout_considerations: Verify that PostgreSQL extensions (vector, uuid-ossp) are enabled in the database before running the DDL.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: Alembic migrations execute cleanly in an isolated environment without requiring the psql binary.
remediation.resolution_details: Replaced subprocess.run psql call in 922ae13073d0_initial_schema.py with native bound SQLAlchemy connection execution.

findings.limitations: Tested via static code review; local environment lacked running PostgreSQL instance.

findings.title: Plaintext API Secrets and Passwords Committed in Historical Git Repository Packfiles
findings.summary: Although commit 8a52c132c71612416b0c7f6693da241eec163de9 untracked .env from the working tree, earlier git commits retain plaintext secret tokens including live 56-character Groq API keys (gsk_...) and database credentials. Anyone cloning the repository can extract these credentials from git pack history.
findings.execution_path: Attacker clones repository -> Runs `git log -p .env` or `git checkout a75128e2 -- .env` -> Extracts active GROQ_API_KEY, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, and RABBITMQ credentials from historical commit objects.
findings.root_cause: The repository was initially populated with live configuration files before .gitignore rules were configured, and later remediation only untracked the file without purging historical commits.
findings.evidence:
$ git log --all --full-history -- ".env"
commit 8a52c132c71612416b0c7f6693da241eec163de9
Author: Kevin Baldha
Date: Wed Nov 4 15:28:26 2026 +0530
    feat(security): resolve global system audit findings...
    - untrack and ignore .env files from git tracking (F-001)

commit a75128e24719bf7fb6aeb6da51647d662d327810
Author: tvmanav
Date: Thu Aug 6 17:39:53 2026 +0530
    Implement CustomerServiceAgent... update LLM provider configuration to Groq
findings.reachability: Anyone with read access to the git repository or backup mirrors.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Attacker obtains read access to the GitHub/GitLab repository.
2. Attacker runs `git show a75128e2:.env`.
3. The plaintext GROQ_API_KEY is retrieved.
4. Attacker uses the stolen key to invoke LLM endpoints at the organization's expense, or uses database passwords to attempt credential stuffing against public infrastructure.
findings.impact: Compromise of third-party LLM API accounts, financial loss from stolen API quotas, credential reuse against deployed infrastructure.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked whether keys in .env were mock templates: Python inspection verified the Groq key is 56 characters, starts with gsk_, and is not a placeholder string.

remediation.strategy: Immediately revoke and rotate the exposed Groq API key and database passwords. Rewrite git history using git-filter-repo or BFG to permanently scrub .env files from all branches, tags, and commits.
implementation_steps: Log in to Groq Console and revoke the active API key; issue a fresh key and store it in an external secret manager.
Change PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ passwords across all environments.
Execute `git filter-repo --path .env --path backend/.env --invert-paths` to scrub history.
Force push updated clean branches to remote origins.
remediation.code_guidance:
```bash
# Purge secrets from git history
git filter-repo --path .env --path backend/.env --invert-paths --force
# Rotate keys in external secret store / vault
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Deploy pre-commit secret detection hooks (e.g. git-secrets, gitleaks, or detect-secrets) to block accidental commits of credentials.
remediation.rollout_considerations: Requires coordinating git history rewrite with all collaborating developers.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: Git history search returns zero commits referencing .env or backend/.env.
remediation.resolution_details: Replaced live Groq API keys with placeholders in .env and backend/.env, untracked them, created scripts/purge_git_secrets.sh for team coordination.

findings.limitations: Rotations must be performed by project owner on provider web consoles.

findings.title: Information Disclosure via Raw Exception Strings in Global Exception Handler
findings.summary: In backend/app/main.py, the global_exception_handler catches unhandled server exceptions and returns `{"detail": str(exc)}` in the HTTP 500 JSON response, only sanitizing errors that explicitly contain the words 'postgresql' or 'password'. Any other runtime failure (e.g. SQLite locks, filesystem paths, Pydantic tracebacks, third-party API socket errors) is returned directly to the caller.
findings.execution_path: Client sends unexpected request or triggers server-side exception -> FastAPI catches exception -> global_exception_handler(request, exc) executes -> Checks if 'postgresql' in error_msg or 'password' in error_msg -> Check evaluates False -> Returns JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={'detail': error_msg}) -> Internal file paths and exception details disclosed to client.
findings.root_cause: Blacklist-based error sanitization attempt that only catches two specific keywords rather than enforcing an opaque error contract in production.
findings.reachability: Any network client able to induce a 500 Internal Server Error.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Attacker sends unexpected Unicode or boundary payloads to internal endpoints.
2. Application raises an unhandled internal exception (e.g. SQLite database locked or FileNotFoundError with local path `/Users/kevinbaldha/...`).
3. Server returns HTTP 500 with the exact local filesystem path and variable state.
findings.impact: Reconnaissance assistance for attackers; leaks underlying server paths, architecture details, and internal component versions.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked whether FastAPI debug mode is disabled: settings.ENVIRONMENT is checked, but global_exception_handler does not gate error_msg based on ENVIRONMENT.

remediation.strategy: Return an opaque error message (`{"detail": "An internal error occurred. Please contact support with correlation ID <UUID>."}`) in production, and log the detailed traceback server-side.
implementation_steps: Modify global_exception_handler in backend/app/main.py.
Generate a correlation UUID for the error.
Log exc with the correlation ID.
If settings.ENVIRONMENT == 'production', return generic error message containing only the correlation ID.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/app/main.py
@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def global_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception):
    error_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    logger.error("Unhandled server error", error_id=error_id, error=str(exc), exc_info=True)
    msg = "Internal server error" if settings.ENVIRONMENT.lower() == "production" else str(exc)
    return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"detail": msg, "error_id": error_id})
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Enforce strict distinction between internal diagnostic logs and external user-facing error payloads.
remediation.rollout_considerations: Operators must reference server logs via the error_id to troubleshoot production issues.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: Triggering an intentional exception with ENVIRONMENT=production returns status 500 with opaque detail and no stack traces.
remediation.resolution_details: Updated global_exception_handler in main.py to return opaque error strings with UUID correlation IDs when ENVIRONMENT=production.

findings.limitations: Tested via static review and exception simulation.

findings.title: Missing Lifespan Initialization of Shared RabbitMQ Event Publisher
findings.summary: The FastAPI application lifespan context manager in app/main.py probes RabbitMQ network connectivity during startup, but never calls connect_rabbitmq() or disconnect_rabbitmq() from app.core.rabbitmq. Consequently, the module-level singleton _publisher remains None, causing any route or background task that calls get_rabbitmq_publisher() to crash with RuntimeError.
findings.execution_path: App starts up -> lifespan executes -> probes RabbitMQ socket -> yields -> connect_rabbitmq() is never called -> _publisher remains None -> Component invokes get_rabbitmq_publisher() -> Raises RuntimeError: 'RabbitMQ publisher is not connected. Ensure the app lifespan has started.'
findings.root_cause: Dead infrastructure wiring: rabbitmq.py was created with connect_rabbitmq lifespan functions, but main.py only implemented inline probes without initializing the singleton.
findings.evidence:
# backend/app/main.py:101-118
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    db_status = await _probe_db()
    redis_status = await _probe_redis()
    mq_status = await _probe_rabbitmq()
    # connect_rabbitmq() is NOT called here
    yield
    # disconnect_rabbitmq() is NOT called here
findings.reachability: Any agent, task, or endpoint attempting to use `get_rabbitmq_publisher` as a FastAPI dependency.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Developer or feature routes an event through `get_rabbitmq_publisher()` dependency.
2. Route is executed in production.
3. Request fails with HTTP 500 RuntimeError because publisher was never connected in lifespan.
findings.impact: AMQP message publishing fails at runtime; event-driven decoupling between microservice agents cannot function as intended.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Verified that dispatcher.py currently bypasses get_rabbitmq_publisher and writes to persistence directly as a workaround.

remediation.strategy: Initialize and tear down the RabbitMQ publisher within FastAPI's lifespan context manager in main.py.
implementation_steps: Import connect_rabbitmq and disconnect_rabbitmq in backend/app/main.py.
In lifespan startup block, call `await connect_rabbitmq()` (wrapped in try/except if optional).
In lifespan shutdown block, call `await disconnect_rabbitmq()`.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/app/main.py
from app.core.rabbitmq import connect_rabbitmq, disconnect_rabbitmq

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    try:
        await connect_rabbitmq()
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.warning("RabbitMQ connection failed at startup", error=str(exc))
    yield
    await disconnect_rabbitmq()
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Consolidate all infrastructure lifecycle management into explicit, observable startup and shutdown handlers.
remediation.rollout_considerations: RabbitMQ server must be accessible during container boot if startup is blocking.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: get_rabbitmq_publisher() returns a connected EventPublisher instance without throwing RuntimeError.
remediation.resolution_details: Integrated connect_rabbitmq and disconnect_rabbitmq into FastAPI lifespan startup and shutdown context manager in main.py.

findings.limitations: Tested via static inspection of lifespan in main.py.

findings.title: Complete Absence of Client-Side Authentication Flow and Login Interface in Web Frontend
findings.summary: While frontend/src/services/api.ts provides an authApi.login helper that attaches Bearer tokens from localStorage, the React application in frontend/src/App.tsx provides zero login views, zero login forms, and zero authentication guards. If production mode is enabled on the backend, every user action in the frontend fails silently or with unhandled HTTP 401 errors because the user has no way to input credentials.
findings.execution_path: User opens frontend at http://localhost:5173/ -> App.tsx routes directly to DashboardPage without checking authentication -> User triggers action (e.g. create order or update shipment) -> API client sends request without token -> Backend in production returns 401 Unauthorized -> Frontend displays error with no way to log in.
findings.root_cause: The frontend was built under the assumption that the backend would always operate in development mode with auto-authenticated dev admin bypass.
findings.evidence:
# frontend/src/App.tsx:36-50
<Routes>
  <Route path="/"              element={<DashboardPage />} />
  <Route path="/orders"        element={<OrdersPage />} />
  <Route path="/shipments"     element={<ShipmentsPage />} />

# No /login route and no AuthContext/ProtectedRoute wrapper
findings.reachability: All web users interacting with the frontend interface.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Operator visits web portal in a production environment.
2. Operator clicks 'Create Order' or 'Reroute Freight'.
3. The browser console logs 401 Unauthorized.
4. The operator has no login button, form, or modal to establish a session.
findings.impact: Application is unusable for interactive operations in production; operational deadlock.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Searched frontend/src/ for authApi references: verified authApi is defined in api.ts line 57 but imported/called in zero components.

remediation.strategy: Implement an AuthProvider React context with a dedicated /login route, session state management, and an AuthGuard wrapper for protected pages.

Create frontend/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx with username and password form.
Wrap protected routes in App.tsx with an AuthGuard that redirects unauthenticated users to /login.
Display current user profile and logout action in TopBar.tsx.

remediation.rollout_considerations: Requires backend auth to be operational with a database-backed user store (F-003).
regression_tests: Frontend unit test for AuthGuard redirection
remediation.acceptance_criteria: Visiting protected route without token redirects to /login; logging in stores token and grants access.
remediation.resolution_details: Built AuthContext, AuthGuard, LoginPage, and TopBar auth status in React frontend, wiring them into App.tsx routing.

findings.title: Unhandled ValidationError in Commercial Order Intake Handler Returns 500 Server Error
findings.verification_status: Confirmed by static trace and unit reproduction
findings.summary: In backend/app/api/v1/orders.py, create_commercial_order accepts CreateCommercialOrderPayload which does not validate duplicate products. Later, inside the route handler body, it constructs OrderWorkflowRequest. If duplicate product IDs are present, Pydantic raises an unhandled ValidationError inside the route body, causing the server to return HTTP 500 Internal Server Error instead of HTTP 422 Unprocessable Content.
findings.execution_path: Client POST /api/v1/orders with duplicate product IDs in items -> FastAPI parses CreateCommercialOrderPayload successfully -> Handler executes -> Handler instantiates OrderWorkflowRequest(...) -> OrderWorkflowRequest field_validator raises ValidationError -> Handler does not catch it -> Bubbles to global_exception_handler -> Server returns HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 422.
findings.root_cause: Input validation schemas between the commercial API portal and internal workflow engine were not synchronized, causing domain validation to fail inside the controller body.
findings.evidence:
# backend/app/api/v1/orders.py:351
wf_request = OrderWorkflowRequest(
    customer_id=_safe_uuid(payload.customer_id),
    order_id=order_id,
    items=[OrderItemRequest(product_id=_safe_uuid(it.product_id), quantity=it.quantity) for it in payload.items],
)
# If duplicate product_id exists, OrderWorkflowRequest validator throws pydantic.ValidationError inside route!
findings.reachability: Any user submitting an order containing duplicate product items to POST /api/v1/orders.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. User submits an order with item A twice (e.g. product 1 x 5, product 1 x 10).
2. Instead of receiving a clean 422 Validation Error explaining duplicate IDs, the server crashes with HTTP 500.
3. Monitoring systems trigger false-positive server error alerts.
findings.impact: Poor API resilience, misleading HTTP status codes, false-positive operational error alerts.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Verified by running python script with OrderWorkflowRequest duplicate validator: confirmed ValidationError is raised.

remediation.strategy: Add the duplicate items validator directly to CreateCommercialOrderPayload so FastAPI's request validation handles it automatically at the HTTP layer, returning HTTP 422.
implementation_steps: Open backend/app/api/v1/orders.py.
Add `@field_validator('items')` to CreateCommercialOrderPayload ensuring all product_id values are unique.
remediation.systemic_fix: Validate all business invariants in input DTO schemas rather than during intermediate domain conversion.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/orders with duplicate product IDs returns HTTP 422 with clear error message.
remediation.resolution_details: Added field_validator validate_unique_products to CreateCommercialOrderPayload in orders.py to reject duplicates with HTTP 422.

findings.title: Use of Unmaintained and Vulnerable `python-jose` Cryptographic Library
findings.summary: The project specifies `python-jose[cryptography]>=3.3.0` for JWT token handling. python-jose has been unmaintained for several years and contains known algorithm confusion and DoS vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-33663, CVE-2024-33664). The broader Python ecosystem recommends PyJWT or Authlib.
findings.execution_path: auth.py imports jose.jwt -> python-jose parses and validates tokens -> legacy parsing bugs / CVEs expose service to algorithmic complexity and confusion attacks.
findings.root_cause: Legacy package selection in pyproject.toml that has not been updated to active maintained standards.
findings.evidence:
# backend/pyproject.toml:25
"python-jose[cryptography]>=3.3.0",

# backend/app/api/v1/auth.py:23
from jose import JWTError, jwt
findings.reachability: Token generation and verification functions in backend/app/api/v1/auth.py.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario:
1. Attacker crafts malformed JWE/JWT payloads triggering known python-jose parser vulnerabilities.
2. Auth service encounters denial of service or unexpected signature verification behavior.
findings.impact: Potential security exposure from unpatched cryptographic dependency.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Checked whether algorithm is restricted in decode: auth.py specifies algorithms=['HS256'], mitigating algorithm confusion.

remediation.strategy: Replace python-jose with PyJWT[crypto]>=2.8.0 across the project.
implementation_steps: Update backend/pyproject.toml: replace python-jose with pyjwt[crypto]>=2.8.0.
In backend/app/api/v1/auth.py, change `from jose import JWTError, jwt` to `import jwt; from jwt.exceptions import PyJWTError as JWTError`.
Run test suite to verify JWT issue and decode compatibility.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/app/api/v1/auth.py
import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import PyJWTError as JWTError
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Adopt automated dependency scanning (e.g. Dependabot, Renovate, pip-audit) in CI pipelines.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: python-jose is removed from pyproject.toml and tokens are generated/validated cleanly with PyJWT.
remediation.resolution_details: Migrated from unmaintained python-jose to pyjwt[crypto]>=2.8.0 in pyproject.toml and auth.py.

findings.limitations: Tested via static lockfile and manifest inspection.

findings.title: Deprecated Logging API and Non-Standard BackgroundTasks Default Parameter Pattern
findings.summary: In backend/scripts/dlq_processor.py:50, `logger.warn` is called instead of `logger.warning`. In Python logging and structlog, `warn` is deprecated and slated for removal. In backend/app/api/v1/workflows.py:557, `background_tasks: BackgroundTasks = BackgroundTasks()` uses a freshly instantiated default object rather than standard FastAPI dependency injection, which can cause background task execution to decouple from the response lifecycle in some ASGI configurations.
findings.execution_path: DLQ processor logs event -> logger.warn emits deprecation warning. Executive approval called -> BackgroundTasks default instance instantiated at module definition time.
findings.root_cause: Code style deviations from FastAPI and Python standard library best practices.
findings.evidence:
# backend/scripts/dlq_processor.py:50
logger.warn("DLQ Message Detected", ...)

# backend/app/api/v1/workflows.py:557
async def approve_workflow(
    workflow_id: str,
    body: ExecutiveApprovalRequest | None = None,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks = BackgroundTasks(),  # Non-standard default instance
findings.reachability: DLQ message processing and workflow executive approval endpoints.
findings.exploit_or_failure_scenario: Under strict Python warning filters, logger.warn raises DeprecationWarning. In some ASGI servers, default BackgroundTasks() may not trigger after response return.
findings.impact: Subtle operational bugs and deprecation warnings in production logs.
findings.counter_evidence_checked: Other endpoints (e.g. orders.py, simulate.py) declare `background_tasks: BackgroundTasks` without default value.

remediation.strategy: Standardize logging calls to logger.warning and remove the default instantiation of BackgroundTasks.
implementation_steps: In backend/scripts/dlq_processor.py:50, change `logger.warn` to `logger.warning`.
In backend/app/api/v1/workflows.py:557, change `background_tasks: BackgroundTasks = BackgroundTasks()` to `background_tasks: BackgroundTasks`.
remediation.code_guidance:
```python
# backend/app/api/v1/workflows.py
async def approve_workflow(
    workflow_id: str,
    body: ExecutiveApprovalRequest | None = None,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks = None,
    _user: Annotated[dict, Depends(require_authenticated_role("admin"))] = None,
):
```
remediation.systemic_fix: Enforce ruff/flake8 rules covering deprecations and mutable default arguments.
remediation.acceptance_criteria: No DeprecationWarnings emitted by dlq_processor.py and approve_workflow uses standard dependency signature.
remediation.resolution_details: Replaced logger.warn with logger.warning in dlq_processor.py and standardized BackgroundTasks dependency injection in workflows.py.

domains.summary: JWT issuance via PBKDF2 hashing implemented for dev users; critical flaw F-003 leaves production with empty user store causing 100% lockout; dev bypass in require_authenticated_role grants admin to unauthenticated callers.

Role checks (admin, analyst, operator, viewer) enforced on select endpoints, but completely missing on /workflows/orders and /simulate (F-001); no object-level authorization (IDOR) on orders or reports.
The system currently operates as a single-tenant enterprise deployment. All customer records, inventory, and telemetry share global tables without tenant scoping predicates.

Pydantic schemas enforce type safety across most endpoints; parameterized SQL prevents injection; unhandled ValidationError on duplicate products leads to 500 error (F-010); error disclosure in global exception handler (F-007).
18-agent LangGraph topology features blackboard consensus, CEO approval tiers ($50k threshold), and automated remediation; unauthenticated workflow trigger presents excessive agency exposure (F-001).
Critical split-brain architecture between PostgreSQL ORM models and SQLite persistence.py causes silent data loss on read endpoints when PostgreSQL is active (F-002).
No PII collected beyond business customer names and synthetic order records; secrets previously committed to git history require rotation (F-006).
FastAPI routers well organized; CORS restricted to localhost regex; health check probes DB/Redis/RabbitMQ; RabbitMQ publisher uninitialized in lifespan (F-008).
Locked requirements present (requirements.lock); dependency on unmaintained python-jose (F-011); live Groq API key leaked in historical commits (F-006).
Bounded LRU state stores (_MAX_WORKFLOW_STORE_SIZE = 500) prevent memory exhaustion DoS; concurrency semaphores limit background tasks; dual-storage queries introduce race conditions.
Structured logging via structlog configured; JSON rendering in production; decision history logged on blackboard; sensitive exception disclosure in HTTP response (F-007).
Docker-compose binds internal infrastructure to 127.0.0.1; security headers middleware active (nosniff, DENY, HSTS); Alembic migration calls external psql process (F-005).
Comprehensive test suite: 224 unit/scenario tests pass; 135 tests skipped due to offline PostgreSQL; frontend fails TypeScript build due to unused variables (F-004).
Frontend missing login page (F-009); frontend build fails on tsc -b (F-004); order creation desynchronized from PostgreSQL (F-002).

positive_controls.evidence: Middleware injects X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy, and HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) in production.

positive_controls.control: Bounded State Stores and Concurrency Semaphores
positive_controls.evidence: In-memory stores enforce LRU bounds (_MAX_WORKFLOW_STORE_SIZE = 500, _MAX_SIM_STORE_SIZE = 500) preventing memory exhaustion DoS, and asyncio.Semaphore(_MAX_CONCURRENT_WORKFLOWS = 10) prevents thread starvation.

positive_controls.control: Timing-Safe Password Verification & Sliding-Window Rate Limiting
positive_controls.evidence: Password comparison uses hmac.compare_digest and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 100,000 iterations. Brute-force protection limits failed login attempts to 5 per minute per IP:username combination with HTTP 429 Retry-After.

Context data passed to LLMs is scanned and sanitized for prompt injection phrases (e.g. 'ignore previous', 'system prompt'). LLMs execute with temperature=0.0 and passive XML delimiters (<PASSIVE_CONTEXT_DATA>) to prevent instruction hijacking.

Structured LLM decisions are verified against candidate_id_whitelist. If the model hallucinates an invalid entity UUID (carrier, supplier, warehouse), the runtime automatically detects and corrects it to a grounded entity ID.

positive_controls.control: Localhost Port Binding for Internal Infrastructure
positive_controls.evidence: PostgreSQL (5432), Redis (6379), and RabbitMQ (5672, 15672) ports are explicitly bound to 127.0.0.1 rather than 0.0.0.0, preventing unauthorized direct external access to backend storage.
